Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Time: 16:30 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Soundscape - Head of Data Platforms), Marcus Ng (Soundscape - Backend Lead), Priya Shah (Soundscape - Security)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be imperfect)
Soundscape is evaluating Redwood for embeddings + generation. They want a private/VPC option for PII, and are concerned about quotas/rate limits and observability. Discussed SDKs, LangChain adapters, gateway patterns, and dedicated vs hosted fallbacks.

Topics covered: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy, rate limits, VPC, KMS, observability hooks

Action items (auto): Maya to send pricing, Devon to set up benchmark harness, customer to share network details

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um i'm Maya with Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, uh with me is devon our solutions engineer.
[00:22] Lena Ortiz: hey Maya, thanks. we have about 45 minutes, i'll give a quick context, and then i want to dig into the gateway piece and rate limiting, because that's... kind of the blocker for us.
[00:35] Devon Park: awesome, sounds good. do you want us to kick off with a brief outline of how teams typically integrate? or do you prefer we jump to your architecture?
[00:44] Lena Ortiz: architecture please. quick context: Soundscape is building a searchable audio index, customers upload audio, we do transcription + embeddings + semantic search and then a small generation step for summaries. we use LlamaIndex for the retrieval glue, langchain orchestration in a few services.
[01:10] Marcus Ng: and we have an edge gateway that handles uploads and routes to internal microservices. currently auth is JWT via an internal STS and per-team API keys.
[01:24] Priya Shah: security context for me: audio can include PII, so we need a private deployment option (VPC), KMS for key rotation, and audit logs retained for 1 year. SOC2 is a table stakes.
[01:40] Maya Chen: totally understood. Redwood supports hosted for fast onboarding, dedicated reserved pools for guaranteed throughput, and private VPC deployments for regulated data. for compliance we have SOC 2, and we can provide audit logs and KMS integrations — i'll add the security pack docs after.
[02:05] Marcus Ng: quick question on flow — we want to keep the gateway in front of our services and just call the Redwood API from a backend service. is there a recommended proxy or sidecar approach?
[02:18] Devon Park: yes, there are a few patterns. the simplest is the edge gateway --> internal microservice that calls Redwood over egress. for lower latency and rate limiting per-team, some customers run a small sidecar on the service host which handles batching, caching prefixes and per-key quotas. we've also seen a proxy pattern where you front Redwood with your own rate limiter and route to Dedicated pools.
[02:46] Lena Ortiz: sidecar sounds attractive, because we can keep quotas closer to the team. does Redwood have a sidecar lib or example?
[02:55] Devon Park: we have SDK examples for Python and Node that show local batching and KV-cache primitives. i'll attach the LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter sample as well — note that the adapter shows how to stream tokens back into LlamaIndex and where to hook prefix caching. it's in our GitHub examples.
[03:18] Lena Ortiz: great. two more orbiting concerns — rate limits/quotas and streaming. we need per-route quotas, per-team quotas, and a way to throttle back-off gracefully without impacting UX.
[03:32] Maya Chen: on quotas: Redwood supports per-api-key quotas, and you can configure per-route overrides in Dedicated. Hosted has shared limits but we can allocate token quotas per API key in the console. you can set hard limits and soft alerts. would you expect quotas to be enforced at your gateway or at Redwood?
[03:50] Marcus Ng: we prefer enforcement at our gateway so we can return custom error codes and do circuit-breaker behavior, but we'd like fallback to hosted or degrade to smaller models if capacity is exceeded.
[04:02] Devon Park: that's a pattern we support — you enforce at the gateway and have a routing policy that points to Dedicated first, with fallback to hosted compatible model variants. routing can be based on latency SLOs or cost tiers. the SDK exposes a retry/backoff helper so the sidecar can implement exponential backoff and fallbacks for streaming calls.
[04:25] Priya Shah: about streaming — can we get partial transcripts or progressive embeddings during the upload pipeline? latency is important for our live features.
[04:36] Devon Park: yes, streaming is supported. for generative endpoints you can stream partial tokens. for embeddings we recommend flushing small batches to reduce tail latency; we also have an embeddings batch endpoint that returns as they are computed. caching helps a lot for repeated prefixes in retrieval-augmented calls.
[04:58] Lena Ortiz: important: where does KV cache live for Dedicated? is it shared across instances? we want consistent cache across pools to avoid stale responses.
[05:10] Devon Park: good question. for Dedicated we provide a distributed KV cache co-located with the pool. it's consistent for that pool; across pools you'd either rely on your own shared cache (e.g., redis) or use routing policies to pin a user to a pool. we call that "pin by session" pattern. note: there's a warm-up time for cold KV entries which can increase first-call latency.
[05:36] Marcus Ng: if we pin sessions to a pool, how does that affect failover — if the pool is down or scaled down, can requests be re-routed and still find relevant cache?
[05:47] Devon Park: re-routing to a different pool will miss local KV entries; you'd either rehydrate from your shared store or accept a slight quality drop. some teams use a hybrid: small LRU local cache + central redis for long-tail.
[06:03] Maya Chen: quick sidebar: for large-scale search workloads our Optimize tool can recommend batching and quantization profiles to reduce cost with minimal quality impact; if you want, devon can run a quick estimation based on your avg token per request.
[06:18] Lena Ortiz: yes please, we'll want cost profiling. our volume is unpredictable — peak is about 400 rps for ingestion during large events, average generation calls maybe 15 rps, embeddings spiky.
[06:33] Marcus Ng: on ingress egress, we use GCP and have a VPC we can peer. what's the networking setup for Private deployments?
[06:43] Devon Park: Private runs in a customer VPC in supported regions or as an on-prem bundle. we support VPC peering and private interconnects; KMS integration works with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM). for peering we exchange CIDR and set up routing, and for some customers we use vpn tunnels.
[07:02] Priya Shah: we require bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and hardware-backed keys for the most sensitive bits. is that available?
[07:11] Maya Chen: yes, BYOK with HSM is available on Private. we'll include the compliance whitepaper and a sample KMS configuration.
[07:22] Lena Ortiz: ok, back to SDKs and adapters. we rely heavily on LlamaIndex and LangChain. do you have first-class adapters or do we need custom glue code?
[07:34] Devon Park: we have maintained adapters for common stacks: a LangChain connector that supports streaming, and a LlamaIndex example that uses the Redwood token streaming hooks. the adapter includes cache hook points and retriever examples. it's not an official "managed" plugin but it's maintained by our integration team.
[07:56] Marcus Ng: any latency numbers you can share for hosted vs dedicated? ballpark for generate at 512 tokens?
[08:06] Maya Chen: ballpark — hosted median latency for a 512-token generation on modern open models is around 300-450 ms per token in streaming scenarios depending on model; dedicated can often get lower tail latency because of pinned instances and warm caches. i'll caveat that with model choice, quantization, and seq length. we also publish perf profiles for common models in the console.
[08:30] Lena Ortiz: can we rate-limit at sub-second granularity? we need to protect the embedding service from bursty uploads.
[08:40] Devon Park: for most setups the gateway enforces per-request throttling; Redwood can do token-based leaky-bucket quotas and burst tokens. if you need sub-second throttling, do it at the gateway sidecar — the SDK has helpers to surface penalties and retry-after headers.
[08:58] Priya Shah: audit logs — what fields are available? we need request id, API key, model served, timestamp, user id, and redaction flags.
[09:09] Maya Chen: audit logs include request id, model, user api key, timestamp, and response size. we can configure PII redaction in Private. retention windows are configurable for Dedicated/Private. i'll add the sample log schema in the follow-up email.
[09:26] Marcus Ng: curious — do you expose OpenTelemetry spans or is it only exported to datadog/honeycomb?
[09:34] Devon Park: first-class OTel support — you can push spans to your collector; we also have native integrations with Datadog and Honeycomb for traces/metrics. the SDK auto-instruments request spans and exposes hooks for custom attributes like customer_team_id.
[09:51] Lena Ortiz: ok, let's talk about billing and quotas mapping. we want per-team budgets and the ability to lock a team if they exceed a monthly budget.
[10:02] Maya Chen: the console supports budget alerts and hard limits on API keys. for Dedicated you can create sub-keys with per-key quotas and set hard stops that reject further requests. hosted also supports per-key quotas but with shared infra constraints — long-running heavy loads are better on Dedicated.
[10:20] Marcus Ng: do you support rate limit headers with remaining/quota reset times? we'd like to surface them in our dashboard.
[10:27] Devon Park: yes — we return x-rw-remaining, x-rw-reset, and quota-tier headers on rate-limited responses; SDK helpers surface those as well so your gateway can read and react accordingly.
[10:40] Lena Ortiz: excellent. technical deep dive request: we'd like a 1-hour session with devops and infra to map out VPC peering, NAT egress, and firewall rules. can we do that next week?
[10:52] Maya Chen: absolutely, i'll propose times. suggested follow-up date in the sheet is 2026-12-21 for infra deep-dive.
[11:00] Marcus Ng: one more on fallbacks — if Dedicated is saturated and we failover to hosted, is there a quality or model compatibility concern?
[11:11] Devon Park: fallback uses compatible model variants we define in your routing policy. there can be differences in latency and cost. we can pin a hosted model that's functionally equivalent but sometimes the quantization or throughput is different so we recommend smoke tests. that's why the 48-hour benchmark helps.
[11:29] Lena Ortiz: regarding LangChain: do you have an example where we replace the llm wrapper with Redwood's streaming SDK? we want to avoid custom polling.
[11:40] Devon Park: yes — the adapter sample includes a LangChain LLM wrapper that exposes the streaming interface and token callbacks; it also demonstrates how to inject incremental embeddings into LlamaIndex. i'll drop the repo link after the call.
[11:57] Priya Shah: security Q: does Redwood support SAML SSO for console and role-based access control for API key issuance?
[12:07] Maya Chen: yes on both counts. SSO for the console, RBAC for project-level roles, and you can have admins restrict who can create API keys. for Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your identity provider.
[12:23] Marcus Ng: what's the expected lead time for Private deployment? we may need BYOK and HSM provision.
[12:32] Maya Chen: typical lead time is 4-8 weeks depending on region and networking approvals; BYOK with HSM may add a bit of coordination. Dedicated can be much faster — usually within 1-2 weeks for reserved pools.
[12:46] Lena Ortiz: ok that timeline helps. budget question: what's the pricing model for Dedicated? is it purely reserved hourly capacity or do you combine with usage?
[12:57] Maya Chen: Dedicated is based on reserved capacity (monthly commit) plus a small usage overlay for burst; the pilot SOW we propose will outline commit vs burst pricing. hosted is pure usage. we'll share a sample pricing table.
[13:12] Marcus Ng: can we run a proof-of-concept on hosted first to validate quality then lift-and-shift to Dedicated?
[13:20] Devon Park: absolutely — that's a common path. you can prototype on hosted and then migrate traffic to Dedicated with minimal code changes; routing policies and model pins handle the switch.
[13:31] Lena Ortiz: nice. any limits on number of API keys or per-tenant quotas?
[13:38] Maya Chen: no hard limits on API keys; we recommend a key per team/service for observability. per-tenant quotas depend on the plan, but we can create hierarchical quotas for teams.
[13:48] Marcus Ng: let's discuss a concrete benchmark plan: we want 48-hour ingestion + embedding run at 50 RPS baseline with spikes to 400 RPS for 10 minute windows, measure p95 latency and error rate. can you run that?
[14:02] Devon Park: yes, we can provision an isolated Dedicated pilot, run the harness, and provide results. we'll need a sample workload shape and token distribution — lena can provide that.
[14:13] Lena Ortiz: i'll get a CSV with request types, avg tokens, and peak windows.
[14:20] Priya Shah: last security note: we will need a contract clause for breach notification within 72 hours and right to audit for the Private deployment.
[14:30] Maya Chen: we have standard contract language; we can add those clauses for Private. legal can coordinate after we sign an NDA if needed.
[14:39] Devon Park: quick mention: if you want to do local rate-limiting we can share a lightweight sidecar example that respects x-rw-* headers and surfaces metrics to your datadog collector. it's under examples/rate-limiter in the repo.
[14:56] Marcus Ng: perfect. about observability — we run datadog and honeycomb. is there example instrumentation for span names and tag keys?
[15:07] Devon Park: yes, the SDK emits spans named redwood.request with attributes like model.name, customer.team_id, api.key.id, and request.duration_ms. we also emit metrics for token_count and request_errors. you can export to your otel collector.
[15:25] Lena Ortiz: awesome. i think we're close on fit, main things are: 1) pilot SOW and pricing, 2) benchmark run, 3) infra deep dive for VPC peering and BYOK.
[15:36] Maya Chen: sounds right. i'll send a follow-up with the SOW, security pack, link to the LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter, and propose times for the infra deep dive.
[15:47] Marcus Ng: timeline wise we need procurement alignment by early january, so the pilot needs to be run before end of december ideally.
[15:57] Maya Chen: we can aim for that. devon, anything to add?
[16:01] Devon Park: i'll scope the benchmark and the sample harness, plus an example sidecar for rate limiting. i'll include instructions for the LangChain wrapper.
[16:10] Priya Shah: thanks, that helps. we'll review the docs and circle back.
[16:14] Lena Ortiz: ok thanks everyone. recap those next steps and owners?
[16:18] Maya Chen: yes — recap in the follow-up email, and i'll cc legal for the contract asks.
[16:23] Marcus Ng: thanks, bye.
[16:25] (call ends)
